classification.difficultyReason: Work through nested logarithm, root and reciprocal restrictions, distinguishing strict from inclusive endpoints and tracking attainable outputs to establish ranges.

content.prompt: Find the domain and range of the following.

answer.worked:
The logarithm requires $x>0$, and the square root requires $\log(x)\geq0$.

$$\begin{align*}\log(x)&\geq0\\x&\geq1\end{align*}$$

Hence $D=[1,\infty)$. On this domain, $\log(x)$ takes every nonnegative value, so its square root also takes every nonnegative value. Thus $R=[0,\infty)$.

The logarithm's argument must be positive and the denominator must be nonzero.

$$\begin{align*}x+3&>0\\x&>-3\\\log(x+3)&\ne0\\x+3&\ne1\\x&\ne-2\end{align*}$$

Hence $D=(-3,-2)\cup(-2,\infty)$. The denominator takes every nonzero real value on this domain. Its reciprocal therefore takes every nonzero real value, so $R=(-\infty,0)\cup(0,\infty)$.

The square-root denominator must be real and nonzero, so its radicand must be strictly positive.

$$\begin{align*}\log(x-2)&>0\\x-2&>1\\x&>3\end{align*}$$

This also ensures that the logarithm's argument is positive. Hence $D=(3,\infty)$. As $x$ increases through this domain, $\sqrt{\log(x-2)}$ takes every positive value. Its reciprocal also takes every positive value, so $R=(0,\infty)$.

The inner logarithm requires $x>0$, and the outer logarithm requires a positive input.

$$\begin{align*}\log(x)&>0\\x&>1\end{align*}$$

Hence $D=(1,\infty)$. On this domain, $\log(x)$ takes every positive value. Applying the outer logarithm gives every real value, so $R=(-\infty,\infty)$.
